Incident report 2026-0412
Date: 3 March 2026
Location: Entroncamento depot
During shunting, points machine P12 failed to detect the reverse position. Two departing services were held for 25 minutes while a technician hand-cranked the points. No injuries. Severity: medium.

trap: narrative; signal ID must be kept
text: On 14 January 2026 the driver of service 1G32 reported a flickering aspect on signal YK417 at York station. The signal was replaced under a planned possession that night. There was no delay to traffic and the event was logged as low severity.

trap: dd/mm/yyyy date; three items; train itself is not equipment
text: Date of occurrence: 22/09/2025. Place: Crewe North Junction. A freight train passed signal CE112 at danger by approximately 40 metres after the TPWS intervened late. Checks found a defective TPWS loop and a misaligned AWS magnet at the signal. No collision occurred. Classification: high severity.

trap: date explicitly unknown; severity explicitly not assigned
text: Preliminary notice. A level crossing barrier at Tunes was found raised while a regional train approached; the train stopped short of the crossing. The barrier controller has been isolated pending inspection. Date and time are still being confirmed with the signaller's log. Severity has not yet been assigned.

On 8 August 2025 at 17:40 a passenger train derailed at low speed on the approach to Pampilhosa after a rail fracture. The leading bogie struck overhead line mast 214/7, bringing down the catenary. Three passengers were taken to hospital. The incident is rated critical.

Yesterday evening an axle counter section at Reading station failed to reset after a train had cleared it, showing the line as occupied. Trains were routed through the relief lines for about 40 minutes until the axle counter was reset by a technician. Severity: medium.

trap: no location; severity explicitly not assessed
text: On 2 June 2026 the cab radio on unit 158 812 lost its connection to the radio network for about ten minutes while the train was in service. The driver contacted the signaller by other means, as per procedure. Severity: not assessed.

trap: location explicitly not recorded; plural equipment
text: Event date: 19 October 2025. During an inspection run, the onboard ETCS unit of a high-speed train recorded repeated balise read errors, and the train braked to a stand twice. Engineers later found two damaged balises and a loose connector on the balise antenna under the cab. The exact section of line was not recorded. Severity: high.

trap: day and month without year -> null; no equipment
text: On 4 March, trespassers were reported walking between the platforms at Carlisle station. Trains were cautioned through the station for 15 minutes until British Transport Police removed them. Logged as low severity.

trap: serious injury; location with platform detail
text: Date: 27 February 2026. Location: Doncaster station, platform 4. A passenger was struck by a closing door of a departing train after the door interlock failed to prevent departure with an obstructed door. The passenger suffered serious injuries. Severity: critical.

trap: relative date 'last Tuesday night' must stay null
text: Last Tuesday night a track circuit at Preston failed in the occupied state, and the signaller authorised two trains to proceed under caution. During the second movement a points heater fault left the points frozen, and the train stopped short. Classified as high severity because of the degraded-mode working.

trap: detector raised the alarm; wagon is not equipment
text: On 11 May 2026 the hot axle box detector at Aveiro raised an alarm on a container train. The train was stopped and the crew found an overheated axle bearing on the fourth wagon, which was detached. Severity: medium.

trap: Portuguese; date explicitly unknown; severity not classified
text: Comunicação preliminar. Na estação de Coimbra-B, o painel de informação ao público deixou de funcionar e uma porta automática de acesso à plataforma 2 ficou bloqueada. A data exata da ocorrência ainda está a ser apurada. A gravidade ainda não foi classificada.

trap: Portuguese date in words; train name is not equipment
text: Data: 5 de abril de 2026. Local: Porto Campanhã. Durante a entrada na estação, o comboio Alfa Pendular parou devido a uma falha do sistema Convel, seguida de uma avaria no aparelho de mudança de via 23. A circulação na Linha do Norte esteve interrompida durante 90 minutos. Gravidade: alta.

No dia 12 de julho de 2025, em Lisboa Oriente, um validador de bilhetes na entrada norte avariou e foi substituído no mesmo dia. Não houve impacto na circulação. Ocorrência classificada como de gravidade baixa.

trap: earlier unrelated incident date must be ignored
text: On 30 September 2026, signal SN205 at Sintra showed a blank aspect for about 20 minutes because of a failed LED module. A similar fault on the same signal was recorded on 2 February 2024 and closed after the module was replaced. Severity: medium.

trap: long; background dates and uninvolved equipment at another crossing
text: At 07:12 on 16 November 2025 a regional service from Vila Real de Santo António collided with a delivery van on the Bom João level crossing in Faro. The van driver died at the scene; the train driver and four passengers were treated for shock. The crossing was renewed in 2019 and its last scheduled inspection, on 3 November 2025, found no defects. Data downloaded after the collision show that the obstacle detection radar registered the van, but the half barriers had been raised 40 seconds earlier because the crossing controller received a false 'train clear' signal from a faulty treadle. The warning lights extinguished at the same moment as the barriers rose. The neighbouring crossing at Loulé, which uses an older barrier controller and was the subject of a separate inquiry in 2023, operated normally throughout and is not part of this investigation. Traffic on the Algarve line was suspended for six hours while the van was removed and the overhead line was checked; no damage to the overhead line was found. The operator's regional safety team, the infrastructure manager and the national investigation body attended. Under the operator's classification scheme the event is rated critical because of the fatality. A joint investigation will examine the treadle, the crossing controller logic and the maintenance records, and an interim report is expected within 30 days. Until then, the crossing is operating with a speed restriction of 30 km/h and local staff are present during the morning peak.

trap: long; report date and an earlier flood with other equipment are distractors
text: This report was written on 24 August 2026 and covers an event at Cais do Sodré station. On 21 August 2026, shortly after 18:00, a power supply unit in the station equipment room tripped. As a result the departure board in the main concourse went blank and the public address system stopped working for 35 minutes. Train services were not affected, and staff made manual announcements on the platforms using megaphones from the station office until power was restored. Customer information was also posted on the operator's social media channels. For context, the same equipment room was flooded on 9 October 2025, when two drainage pumps failed during heavy rain; that event was investigated separately and the pumps were replaced in November 2025. There is no evidence that the flooding contributed to this failure. The maintenance contractor replaced the power supply unit on the evening of 21 August 2026 and ran a full test of the departure board and the public address system, both of which worked correctly. A review of spare parts held on site has been requested, because the replacement unit had to be brought from Lisboa Oriente. The event has been logged as low severity. No passengers or staff were injured, and no complaints relating to the outage have been received so far.
